episode.title: Pronunciation as a Reliability Signal
episode.description: A. correspondent talks with Renee Montague-Park: Pronunciation as a Reliability Signal.

bullets: Mispronunciation is a high-signal mistake — it signals to listeners that a speaker isn’t paying attention, undermining trust and credibility.
Reliability of voice is partly preparation, partly humility, and the second-order effect is the part most people overlook.
The trade-offs around reliability intersect with every aspect of public radio production, from editorial decisions to team dynamics.
Ignoring the foundational role of humility leads to rebuilding trust and consistency from scratch a year later.
The most underrated piece of public radio is not content or delivery but the consistent, grounded reliability of voice.
Teams using NPR have demonstrated that mispronunciation patterns correlate directly with perceived lack of care or attention.
Listeners detect inconsistencies in voice reliability — especially in tone and precision — long before they notice the content.
Running a single idea for two weeks enables iteration and reveals how small adjustments compound into meaningful improvement.
